To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) bacteria can use nanosized membrane channels to exchange metabolites with neighboring cells, 2) these channels can be used to exchange metabolites that are essential for growth of one of the connected cells, 3) the channels can be induced by the need of a cell to exchange a specific metabolite, and 4) the channels can also be established between two distant bacterial species.
